base_observation: Current bind_completed_reentry passes memory_event only to validate_memory_event_bindings. That validator checks exact CortexEventPacket type, memory_refs cardinality/order, memory_id equality and TypedMemoryRecord<->MemoryLifecycleState validity, but it does not bind the memory event's session_id, turn_id or event_kind to the exact completed heard-result session/turn. The receipt also records lifecycle/typed-memory evidence but no memory_event identity. This packet does not modify any WP717-G3-owned source/test/workflow path.

falsifiers.setup: Build an exact completed heard result for voice session A/turn A. Build a MemoryLifecycleState plus TypedMemoryRecord that satisfy the G3 exact heard-result payload relation and whose memory_id is referenced by a structurally valid CortexEventPacket from different voice session B (or different unrelated turn) while preserving the same memory_refs tuple. Pass that foreign event as memory_event.
falsifiers.failure_signature: The completed reentry receipt admits exact heard-result memory evidence even though the event carrying the memory reference belongs to a different session/turn causal context.
falsifiers.why_high_information: Separates exact lifecycle-payload identity from exact event-level causal identity. A repair that only adds lifecycle.payload_ref/payload_sha256 equality can still pass this counterexample.

falsifiers.setup: Build an exact completed heard result and an otherwise valid exact MemoryLifecycleState/TypedMemoryRecord pair. Construct a valid CortexEventPacket with matching session/turn and the correct memory_refs tuple but use a non-memory event_kind such as ERROR or TOOL_RESULT, then pass it as memory_event.
falsifiers.failure_signature: Any structurally valid CortexEventPacket carrying memory_refs is treated as the authoritative memory-binding event regardless of event_kind.
falsifiers.why_high_information: Tests whether the consumer binds the semantic event class instead of Goodharting on the presence of memory_refs alone.

falsifiers.setup: Create two distinct valid MEMORY_BIND CortexEventPackets for the same session/turn and same exact memory_refs but with different event_id/monotonic_ms/detail. Invoke completed reentry separately with each while all other inputs are identical.
falsifiers.failure_signature: Two causally distinct admitted memory events collapse to the same VoiceHeardResultReentryReceipt because no memory_event id/digest participates in receipt identity, while surrounding claims describe exact event-level memory binding.
falsifiers.why_high_information: Forces an explicit architectural choice: event wrapper is reference-only and must be documented/scoped as such, or exact event identity is causal and must survive into the receipt. It prevents unsupported exact-event claims without forcing a new memory authority.

acceptance_guidance: The G3 mutation owner should consume VSR07E/VSR07F only if current product semantics require the memory_event itself to be causally bound to the completed heard-result session/turn and memory-binding event class. VSR07G is a scope discriminator: either preserve exact admitted memory-event identity in the receipt or explicitly classify the event wrapper as non-authoritative/reference-only and avoid stronger causal claims. Reuse existing CortexEventPacket/MemoryLifecycle/TypedMemory authorities; do not create a second state or memory authority.
next_exact_action: G3 mutation owner refreshes main after VSR07A-D and VSR08 coverage, evaluates VSR07E/F against the repaired subject, and records whether memory_event identity is exact authority or reference-only. Add only the smallest regression/fence required by that decision before repository acceptance; do not dispatch VPS until the materially changed exact subject passes the complete WP717 discriminator set.
